text: Resistance
How readily the defender takes damage. A larger displayed resistance value generally means more damage taken.
Check Attack Type resistance and Sin resistance separately. Their reference value is 1: higher values increase damage, and lower values reduce it.

An ally's Identity determines their base physical resistances, shown in the Slash, Pierce, and Blunt columns. E.G.O determines Sin resistances. Battle begins with the equipped ZAYIN E.G.O's resistances; after an E.G.O attack finishes, its Sin resistances replace the current ones.
Final damage combines both resistances with other modifiers. The displayed values are not direct ratios of final damage.

Fragile and Protection modify skill damage taken for 1 turn. They do not rewrite the resistance table and are handled separately in damage calculation. Affinity-specific versions apply only to the named affinity.
Exploiting a weakness does not necessarily improve Clash odds. Damage and Clash Power are different.
Do not read ×0.5 as guaranteed half damage or ×2.0 as guaranteed double damage.
The Fragile status is a separate damage-taken effect; do not confuse it with a resistance label.
Resistance values and their effect on damage
×0.5: reduces damage
×1.0: reference value
×2.0: increases damage
Bar length compares displayed resistance values, not final damage ratios. The other resistance and level differences also affect calculation.
Fragile, Protection, and damage modifiers
Resistance affects damage effectiveness; Fragile and Protection temporarily modify damage taken.
Each 1 Fragile increases damage taken by 10%; each 1 Protection reduces it by 10%. Both normally cap at 10 and last for 1 turn. Other modifiers still affect final damage.
Damage Up and Damage Down modify the attacker's skill damage. If an affinity is specified, only that affinity is affected.
Unlike Power modifiers, these do not directly determine Clash results. Distinguish Clash Power, Attack Power, and damage effects.
Resistance, Fragile, Protection, and damage modifiers are only parts of the calculation. One value alone does not determine final damage.
Separate the stages of modification
Clash Power: affects who wins the Clash
Damage Up: modifies the attacker's damage
Fragile and Protection: modify the defender's skill damage taken
Check the named affinity for affinity-specific effects. See damage calculation for how modifiers combine.
Potency and Count
Values describing a status effect's strength and remaining activations or duration. When Count decreases depends on the effect.
Some statuses track Potency and Count separately. Inflicting Potency and increasing Count are different changes.
Burn normally activates at Turn End; Rupture activates when the bearer is hit. Check each effect's trigger and when its Count decreases.
Stacking, caps, and Count consumption differ between effects. Read each description rather than assuming one universal rule.
2 Count does not necessarily mean 2 turns remaining.
Skill Power and status Potency are separate values.
Ordinary Rupture: 5 Potency, 2 Count
Take a hit: 5 additional damage
Count falls from 2 to 1
After the next activation, Count runs out
Assumes no effects that change Potency or Count during the sequence and no special modifiers.
Burn
A status that deals damage at Turn End. Potency determines damage per activation; Count tracks duration.
Ordinary Burn deals fixed damage equal to its Potency at Turn End, then loses 1 Count.
Increasing Potency and increasing Count are different effects. Turn End, rather than the number of attack hits, is its normal trigger.
Even fixed damage can interact with special enemy effects that reduce Burn damage.
Related effects such as Dark Flame do not necessarily follow the same rules.
Burn maintained at 5 Potency and 2 Count
First Turn End: 5 damage, Count 2 → 1
Second Turn End: 5 damage, Count 1 → 0
No additional applications, consumption, Burn damage modifiers, or special effects occur in this example.

Bleed
A status that damages its bearer when they roll attack-skill Coins.
Ordinary Bleed deals fixed damage equal to its Potency when an attack Coin is rolled, then loses 1 Count after the roll.
Unlike Rupture, it does not wait for an enemy attack to hit the bearer. Bleed also activates during Clashes, so watch when the bearer acts.
Do not simply count simultaneous Clash rolls and sequential attack rolls as identical numbers of activations.
Ordinary defense skills do not trigger Bleed in the same way as attack skills.
A Bleeding unit rolls an attack Coin
The unit has Bleed
The unit rolls an attack Coin
The unit takes Bleed damage and loses Count
The unit here is the bearer of Bleed. The roll triggers it regardless of Heads or Tails.
Tremor
A status normally used to raise Stagger Thresholds through Tremor Burst. Applying it alone does not deal damage.
When an attack triggers Tremor Burst, ordinary Tremor raises Stagger Thresholds according to its Potency. Its Count falls by 1 after Turn End.
Distinguish applying Tremor from triggering Tremor Burst. Amplitude Conversion and similar effects can change its behavior.
Do not treat Tremor Potency as ordinary additional damage.
Read each converted Tremor effect separately, even if its name still includes Tremor.

Rupture
A status that deals damage separately from the normal attack when its bearer is hit.
Ordinary Rupture deals fixed damage equal to its Potency when the bearer is hit by an attack skill, then loses 1 Count.
It ends when Count runs out, so maintain Count as well as Potency. Unlike Bleed, it does not wait for the bearer's own attack Coin rolls.
2 Count does not mean a duration of 2 turns.
Check enemy-specific modifiers such as Rupture damage reduction separately.
Ordinary Rupture: 5 Potency, 2 Count
First hit: 5 additional damage, Count 2 → 1
Second hit: 5 additional damage, Count 1 → 0
Normal attack damage is excluded. There are no additional applications, consumption, or special modifiers.
Sinking
A status that damages SP when its bearer takes attack damage. It behaves differently against targets without SP.
Ordinary Sinking deals SP damage equal to its Potency when the bearer takes damage from an attack skill, then loses 1 Count.
Against targets without SP, it deals Gloom damage instead. A target at 0 SP is different from one that has no SP at all.
SP damage is not automatically HP damage.
Against targets without SP, account for Gloom resistance and other relevant modifiers.
Sinking behaves differently depending on the target
A target with Sinking takes attack damage
Has SP: takes SP damage
Has no SP: takes Gloom damage
In either branch, ordinary Sinking loses 1 Count after activation. Separate effects such as Sinking Deluge are excluded.
Poise
A status whose Potency raises Critical Hit chance. Count governs activation and persistence.
Ordinary Poise gives 5% Critical Hit chance per 1 Potency. A Critical Hit adds a modifier to damage calculation.
Count falls by 1 after a Critical Hit and at Turn End. High Potency cannot sustain the effect once Count runs out.
Poise Potency does not directly increase Coin Power.
A Critical Hit does not always multiply final damage by 1.2. Account for Identity-specific bonuses and conditions.
10 Poise Potency: ordinary Critical Hit chance
10 Poise Potency
A half chance, not a guarantee
Assumes Poise Count remains and there are no special chance modifiers. Critical Hit chance and Coin Heads chance are separate.
Charge
A stored resource used for skill conditions and costs. Having Charge does not universally strengthen attacks.
Ordinary Charge Count can stack up to 20 and falls by 1 at Turn End. Skills use it according to their own requirements and costs.
Thresholds and consumption differ by Identity and skill. Some special effects check Charge Potency rather than Count; read them separately.
Charge Count is separate from the Sin resources used for E.G.O.
Identity-specific descriptions take precedence for special caps, upkeep, and consumption rules.
Check Charge Count before choosing a skill
Check current Charge Count
Compare it with the skill's requirement and cost
Choose a skill whose condition is met
Do not assume every Identity needs the same Charge Count. Account for the decrease at Turn End.
Paralyze
A debuff that fixes the Coin Power of a stated number of the target's Coins at 0 for 1 turn.
1 Paralyze fixes the Coin Power of 1 Coin used that turn at 0. It does not directly reduce Base Power or Final Power by 1.
A paralyzed positive Coin adds no Power even on Heads. A paralyzed negative Coin loses its usual subtraction, so Paralyze can sometimes prevent a Power decrease.
Paralyze is consumed in Coin-use order. Coins used during a Clash can consume it first; whether any remains for the attack depends on Coin count and Clash results.
Do not confuse Paralyze stacks with the skill's remaining Coins. Check specific descriptions when Unbreakable Coins or Coin effects are involved.
Paralyze affects Coin Power
Positive Coin: the paralyzed Coin adds nothing on Heads
Negative Coin: negative Coin Power becomes 0
Check Base Power and other Power modifiers separately
The order in which Paralyze is applied, and its handling during Clashes and attacks, depend on the skill's current state.
